box.count-bounds.description: How many, from min to max, either left out

box.count-range.description: How many: a count, `4`, or a range, `{ min = 2, max = 8 }`, either end left out

oneOf.description: How many, from min to max, either left out

box.disk.description: `disk`: how big, and how fast, as `{ min = "40 GB", type = "fast" }`

min.description:
Its least size, such as `"40 GB"`: what the box gets unless its
image needs more, as NVIDIA's images for a box with GPUs do. 20 GB
by default.

type.description: How fast: `balanced` (gp3 on AWS, pd-balanced on Google Cloud), the default, or `fast` (io2 at 50 IOPS a GB, or pd-ssd), billed for its speed too.

box.gpu-bounds.description: How many GPUs, from min to max, and which model

model.description: Which GPU: a model alone means at least one

box.gpus.description: How many GPUs: a count, `1`, or at least min, at most max, of a model, `{ min = 1, max = 2, model = "nvidia-l4" }`

oneOf.description: How many GPUs, from min to max, and which model

box.isolation.description: How a box made here is isolated: in its sandbox, the default, or directly. A box in a cloud account is a machine of its own, so it refuses the whole table.

no_sandbox.description:
Whether it runs directly, with your own access and no sandbox;
refused where this machine's policy says `unsandboxed = false`.

sandbox.description:
The sandbox specification it runs in; given with no file, it only runs in
its sandbox again.

vm.description:
A VM specification, for a workload in a VM, relative to its file. This
build has no VM provider, so a file naming one is refused, never
run in a sandbox instead.
vm.x-link-unavailable: this build of Link has no VM provider

login.description:
Whether the box's `lnk` signs in to your Link account, which a box
made for a service turns off with `false`.

version.description:
The `lnk` release to install with its modules, such as `0.14.0` or
a prerelease, 0.11.0 or later. From a file it can't be behind this
computer's `lnk`, so a specification someone hands you can't install a
release with a known hole; `--lnk.version` given yourself can.
Left out, the latest.

additionalProperties.description: `[machine]`: its fields, and each cloud's own table, `[machine.<cloud>]`, by the cloud's kind (`aws`, as `lnk cloud list` says): every key of `[machine]`, replacing it on that cloud, and the only place for region and size

box.machine.description: `[machine]`: its fields, and each cloud's own table, `[machine.<cloud>]`, by the cloud's kind (`aws`, as `lnk cloud list` says): every key of `[machine]`, replacing it on that cloud, and the only place for region and size

cpus.description: How many CPUs: a count, `4`, or a range, `{ min = 2, max = 8 }`. Left out, the default size's.

disk.description: The boot disk: how big, and how fast. Left out, 20 GB, `balanced`.

gpus.description: How many GPUs, and which model. Left out, none.

memory.description: How much memory: a size with its unit, `"8 GB"`, or a range of them, `{ min = "4 GB", max = "16 GB" }`. Left out, the default size's.

region.description:
Where the box is made: a cloud's region, or on Google Cloud a zone
in it, in a cloud's own table only. `--zone` with `--cloud` sets
the named cloud's. Left out, the account's.

size.description:
A machine type, such as `t3.large`, in a cloud's own table only, in
place of `cpus`, `memory` and `gpus`, which it has built in. Left
out, the smallest that fits is picked.

spot.description:
Whether it's a spot machine: cheaper, but the cloud may stop it and
start it again. `false` by default.

tags.description:
Your tags on the machine and its disk, at most 40, each key
starting with a lowercase letter, keys and values lowercase
letters, digits and dashes. Keys starting `lnk-` or `aws:`, and
`Name`, are Link's or the cloud's, and refused.

box.size-bounds.description: How much, from min to max, each a size with its unit, as `4 GB`, either left out

box.size-range.description: How much: a size with its unit, `"8 GB"`, or a range of them, `{ min = "4 GB", max = "16 GB" }`, either end left out

oneOf.description: How much, from min to max, each a size with its unit, as `4 GB`, either left out

cloud-contract.attach.description: Existing resources attached to the machine, which the box uses and never creates or deletes

address.description: A reserved address it takes: the address's name on Google Cloud; on AWS, its allocation ID. Kept when the box is deleted.

disks.description: Data disks it attaches, never formats and keeps when it's deleted: persistent disks' names on Google Cloud; on AWS, volumes' IDs, each in its subnet's availability zone.

identity.description: Who it acts as in its cloud: a service account's name or email on Google Cloud; on AWS, an instance profile's name.

network.description: The network it joins: a network's name on Google Cloud; on AWS, a subnet's ID whose VPC has an `lnk-box` security group.

cloud-contract.disk-type.description: How fast a box's disk is: `balanced`, or `fast`

core.duration.description: How long: a whole number and ms, s, m, h or d, as 30s, 10m or 2h

core.os.description: A machine's OS, which a box and an environment each name

description: A box specification describes a machine in your own cloud as a TOML file: its CPUs, memory, disk, system and region, the `lnk` installed on it, what it attaches, and how a box made here is isolated

attach.description: Existing resources attached to the machine, which the box uses and never creates or deletes.

deadline.description:
How long the box lives, from one second through seven days, such
as `30m`, `4h` or `7d`. Left out, it lives until it's deleted.

env.description:
The environment file the box is set up from, at every placement,
captured once when the box is made and started again at each `lnk
box start`. Left out, the box has no application setup.

isolation.description: How a box made here is isolated: in its sandbox, the default, or directly. A box in a cloud account is a machine of its own, so it refuses the whole table.

link_tags.description:
Link's own tags on the machine, beside yours, such as the group a
job's boxes are in. Link writes these for its own boxes.

machine.description:
The machine, as you'd describe one at a store: every cloud gets the
smallest that fits, and a cloud's own table, `[machine.<cloud>]`,
replaces any of its keys on that cloud.

name.description:
What its boxes are named after: `web` makes `web-1`, `web-2` and so
on. Lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter,
at most 27. Left out, the account's name; `--name` still names one
box exactly.

self_remove.description:
Whether the machine may remove itself when its work ends, as a box
a job made does.

version.description:
A whole number, yours to bump, which each box remembers it was made
from.
